title: Guilt by Association: Semantic Leakage Drives Associative Gender Bias
abstract: arXiv:2610.28944v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Semantic leakage occurs when a concept in the prompt steers model generation about an entity, even though the concept is irrelevant to it (e.g., a person who likes yellow is said to work as a school bus driver). It has mostly been studied in settings where the concept is directly attributed to the entity the model is asked about. This leaves open whether leakage is a flawed heuristic, where the model builds a profile of that entity, or a much broader associative tendency, e.g., working across seemingly unrelated entities. We argue for the latter: even after removing the attribution of the concept to the specific entity, leakage persists. Next, we extend this idea to gender bias. While work on gender bias in LMs typically looks at cases where the stereotyped concept is attributed to an entity, our findings suggest that a concept may steer outputs with its mere presence in the scene. We show this using gendered concepts under two condition

translated_title: 连带之罪：语义泄漏驱动联想性性别偏见
translated_abstract: 语义泄漏是指提示中的一个概念会引导模型对某个实体的生成内容，即使该概念与该实体无关（例如，喜欢黄色的人被说成是校车司机）。此前的研究大多集中在概念被直接归属于模型所询问的实体的场景中，这就留下了一个未解问题：泄漏到底是一种有缺陷的启发式方法（即模型为该实体构建一个画像），还是一种更广泛的联想倾向（例如，能够在看似不相关的实体之间起作用）？我们支持后一种观点：即使移除概念与特定实体之间的归属关系，泄漏依然存在。接着，我们将这一想法扩展到性别偏见。虽然针对语言模型性别偏见的已有研究通常考察刻板印象概念被归属于某个实体的情况，但我们的发现表明，一个概念仅凭其在场景中的出现就可能引导模型的输出。我们在两种条件下使用带有性别色彩的概念展示了这一点。
tldr: 该论文发现语言模型中的语义泄漏是一种广泛的联想倾向——概念无需被归属于特定实体，仅凭其在输入场景中的出现就能引导模型关于该实体的生成内容，并由此驱动联想性性别偏见。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that semantic leakage is a broad associative tendency—a concept's mere presence in the scene, without any attribution to an entity, can steer model outputs about that entity and drive associative gender bias.
